paper.title: A PRNG specialized in double precision floating point numbers using an affine transition (dSFMT)
paper.venue: Monte Carlo and Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods 2008 (Springer)

program.how: written for ounce-core as plain integer C from the dSFMT recurrence on 128-bit words with a lung word (N=191, POS1=117, SL1=19, SR=12, the two masks of the 19937 parameter set); the fixed-exponent mantissa trick and the range conversions use bit patterns and exact integer fractions, so no floating-point arithmetic is run; the init_gen_rand / init_by_array seeding, exponent mask and period certification were re-implemented from the authors' reference source; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: all 22 sections of the authors' published test output for dSFMT2-19937:117-19 match, 2240 values compared as 15-decimal strings: seed 0 in [1,2) (1000 values); seeds 0 to 19 with the ranges [0,1), (0,1], (0,1), [1,2) in turn (12 values each, 240); init_by_array {1, 2, 3, 4} in [1,2) (1000 values)

expected_values_source.what: the authors' dSFMT.19937.out.txt, the output of their test program test.c (default build)
expected_values_source.note: the values are data, copied as text; the authors' code (dSFMT.c, dSFMT-common.h, params, test.c) was read for constants, seeding and conversions and was not copied. The published file lists only the first 12 values (1000 for two sections) per seed; later outputs are not compared

negative_control: built with -DDSFMT_POS1=116 (POS1 = 116 instead of 117), 0 of 2240 published values match, 0 of 22 sections match, and the program exits 1 (checked on ounce-core Tier-3 and natively)
not_checked: the paper's period (2^19937-1), equidistribution and speed claims, and the other Mersenne exponents
dSFMT's array-fill interface and the 'conversion on the fly' versus bulk-conversion differences (identical sequences, not exercised here)

an actual floating-point (double) execution of the conversions: the check computes the exact decimal value of each double's bit pattern with integers, which is what a correct IEEE implementation prints
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 2240 doubles the authors publish for dSFMT-19937. It does not show the statistical claims hold.
